transcript.text: Yes, Elena. Here is my formal recommendation as assigned litigation counsel: GO — with conditions shaped by the operative contract instruction. Given the AAA commercial arbitration requirement and the limited carve-out permitting a court application only to protect tangible confidential materials, I recommend we pursue a confidential return-and-deletion resolution consistent with Maya's client instructions. Specifically: (1) we send a pre-arbitration demand letter invoking the AAA arbitration clause, seeking return and certified deletion of the tangible confidential materials; (2) we reserve the right to seek a narrow court application under the carve-out solely to protect the tangible confidential materials if the consultant does not comply; (3) we do not assert any non-compete, employment bar, or competitor restriction, as the contract does not authorize these and the client has instructed against them; and (4) we avoid any public court filing at this stage, consistent with client instructions. This approach is contractually permissible and aligns with the client's stated objectives. I'm ready for Maya's recommendation and your final approval, Elena.
